findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify that `RichTextCodec` maps to the existing `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` / `OutboundMapper.map_fields_to_remote` rich-text boundary and `UserIdentityModel` maps to the existing `IdentityConvention` protocol — or if new named types are introduced, specify exactly how they compose with the `Backend` port so DC implements the SAME five role protocols as Cloud and remains exercisable by the existing backend-agnostic contract suite.
evidence: Plan text: 'Pin the two real axes of variation as contracts: a RichTextCodec (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for DC) and a UserIdentityModel (accountId for Cloud, name for DC).'

Existing port in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py`: `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` already covers rich-text decode; `IdentityConvention` already covers the rebar-id back-pointer. Neither `RichTextCodec` nor `UserIdentityModel` exists in the codebase.
AC: '`JiraDataCenterBackend` is exercised by the backend-agnostic contract suite, not only by adapter-local tests.' — requires DC to implement the existing Backend port, not a parallel hierarchy.
findings.finding: The plan introduces `RichTextCodec` and `UserIdentityModel` as the two named contracts pinning DC/Cloud variation, but neither name appears in the existing `Backend` port (`_backend.py`), which already defines `InboundMapper.normalize_rich_text` and `IdentityConvention` for exactly these responsibilities. If the implementer treats `RichTextCodec`/`UserIdentityModel` as new first-class types separate from the existing protocol hierarchy, the DC adapter may end up with a parallel contract structure that bypasses the existing `Backend` port and cannot be exercised by the existing backend-agnostic contract suite — breaking the AC that requires `JiraDataCenterBackend` to be exercised by that suite.
findings.location: Approach section, Step 3: 'Pin the two real axes of variation as contracts: a RichTextCodec (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for DC) and a UserIdentityModel (`accountId` for Cloud, `name` for DC).'

Implementer creates `UserIdentityModel` as a new protocol separate from `IdentityConvention`, causing DC's assignee resolution to live outside the `Backend` port and requiring the contract suite to be separately extended.

Existing codebase hardcodes REST v3 (acli.py:638: /rest/api/3/issue/) and Basic Auth with accountId
No citation in the plan to pycontribs/jira docs, changelog, or issue tracker confirming PAT bearer + REST v2 + wiki-markup support

findings.finding: The plan asserts `pycontribs/jira` 'absorbs DC-vs-Cloud auth, pagination, and payload quirks' (PAT bearer auth, REST v2 dispatch, wiki-markup body encoding) without citing evidence that the library supports all three for Jira Data Center. The existing Cloud adapter uses REST v3 + Basic Auth + accountId explicitly; whether pycontribs/jira cleanly handles the DC-specific PAT bearer token mode, REST v2 endpoint routing, and wiki-markup (vs ADF) payloads is a load-bearing but unverified capability claim.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify how `RichTextCodec` and `UserIdentityModel` relate to the `OutboundMapper` and `IdentityConvention` role Protocols already pinned by ADR 0035 §(d) — state whether they are sub-parameters of those existing protocols, replacements, or new orthogonal contracts, and record this in the amending ADR.
evidence: ADR 0035 §(d) defines OutboundMapper: 'local ticket fields → vendor field/value shapes (+ rich text)' — rich-text encoding is already in scope
ADR 0035 §(d) defines IdentityConvention: 'how the backend stores/reads the rebar-id back-pointer' — but also notes accountId vs name as a Cloud/DC axis
Plan introduces RichTextCodec and UserIdentityModel as new concepts without cross-referencing these existing protocols or explaining whether they replace, extend, or sit below them
findings.finding: The plan introduces two new named contracts — `RichTextCodec` (ADF vs wiki/plain) and `UserIdentityModel` (accountId vs name) — as the primary DC/Cloud variation axes, but does not justify why these are new top-level protocols rather than parameterizations of the `OutboundMapper` and `IdentityConvention` role Protocols that ADR 0035 §(d) already pins. The existing `OutboundMapper` already owns rich-text encoding (map_fields_to_remote, description fitting) and `IdentityConvention` already owns identity (rebar-id back-pointer). Introducing new protocols that overlap these without justification risks re-fragmenting the seam ADR 0035 established.
findings.location: Approach §3: 'Pin the two real axes of variation as contracts: a RichTextCodec … and a UserIdentityModel'
scenarios: Implementers create RichTextCodec separately from OutboundMapper, resulting in two places that own description encoding — the exact duplication the plan is trying to eliminate
The new protocols are never wired into the Backend port defined by ADR 0035 §(d), leaving them as orphan abstractions

findings.finding: The plan relies on 'a Dockerized Jira from the Atlassian SDK at localhost:2990' as the DC integration oracle but does not verify that the Atlassian Plugin SDK Docker image is available and functional for a current Jira Data Center version. The Atlassian Plugin SDK (`atlas-run-standalone`) has had maintenance gaps, and the Docker image it ships has historically been several major versions behind current Jira DC releases. The plan cites `pycontribs/jira`'s `tests/conftest.py` as precedent but does not confirm this image produces a Jira version representative of CMS's actual deployment.

The SDK Docker image is no longer maintained post-Cloud-pivot and `atlas-run-standalone` does not start cleanly, blocking all integration verification
findings.suggested_fix: Consider using the official `atlassian/jira-software` Docker image with a pinned DC LTS version tag (e.g. 9.12-LTS) rather than the Plugin SDK image, which provides a more representative and independently maintained oracle.

findings.finding: The Docker-based integration oracle is underspecified: the plan names 'the Atlassian SDK at localhost:2990' but provides no Docker image name, tag, or startup procedure. 'Atlassian SDK' (the atlas-run/amps Maven plugin) and a plain Docker Hub image (e.g. atlassian/jira-software) are two distinct setups — the former requires a full Maven/SDK toolchain; the latter is a simple `docker run`. pycontribs/jira's conftest.py uses the Docker Hub image, not atlas-run. Without an exact image reference, CI operators cannot reproduce the oracle environment, making the [operator-attested] AC unverifiable.

findings.finding: The plan asserts pycontribs/jira 'already absorbs DC-vs-Cloud auth, pagination, and payload quirks' and will be used as the DC transport, but the specific API surface for PAT bearer auth configuration is unverified. pycontribs/jira supports PAT via the `token_auth` constructor parameter (e.g. `JIRA(server=url, token_auth='<pat>')`), but the plan never names this parameter, the corresponding env var the adapter will read, or how `UserIdentityModel`'s `name`-based user lookup will be driven through the library's user-search API. A flag-level mismatch here (e.g. using `basic_auth` instead of `token_auth`) causes silent auth failures at runtime.

scenarios: The DC adapter is written to pass `basic_auth=(user, pat)` instead of `token_auth=pat`, which Jira DC rejects with a 401 (DC treats a PAT as a bearer token, not a Basic password).

The `UserIdentityModel` for DC needs a `/rest/api/2/user/search?username=<name>` lookup, but the pycontribs/jira method name or signature differs from what the author assumes, causing a runtime AttributeError.

The existing ADF codec in src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/adf.py is a custom implementation; no wiki-markup equivalent exists in the codebase (search returned no matches for 'wiki-markup', 'wiki_markup')

findings.finding: The `RichTextCodec` abstraction for wiki-markup/plain-text (DC) vs ADF (Cloud) is described as a contract the plan will define, but the plan does not verify whether pycontribs/jira exposes wiki-markup body encoding as a usable API surface, or whether the team must write the codec from scratch. Jira REST v2 bodies are plain strings or wiki-markup strings passed as `description` fields directly — pycontribs/jira does not provide a wiki-markup serializer/deserializer. If the team must write the wiki-markup codec, the scope of the DC story is larger than implied.

scenarios: The plan ships `RichTextCodec` with an assumed 'pass-through plain string' DC implementation that later breaks when the description contains Jira wiki-markup formatting that needs round-trip fidelity.
